title: Folding never assigns a free variable
statement: Let $t$ be a term on $n$ variables (a list of literals), let $(k_1,b_1),\dots,(k_m,b_m)$ be a list of pairs in $\bbn\times\mathrm{Bool}$, and let $\rho$ be a restriction on $n$ variables. Process the entries left to right, starting from $\rho$: for the entry $(k_i,b_i)$, delete the first $k_i$ literals of $t$; if nothing remains, leave the current restriction unchanged, and otherwise reset the variable of the first surviving literal to free. Then for every variable $v$ left free by $\rho$, the restriction obtained at the end of this process still leaves $v$ free.
hypotheses_covered: t is a term on n variables (list of literals)
entries is a list of pairs in ℕ × Bool
σ is a restriction on n variables
σ v = none (v is free in the starting restriction)
replaced:
If $\sigma\,v = \mathrm{none}$, then folding the decoder's $\sigma$-update over any list
of entries still gives $\mathrm{none}$ at $v$; the fold never sets a previously unset
variable to a value via the $\sigma$-update.
